title: Why Bad News Stays With You Longer Than Good News
hook: We remember negative feedback far more clearly than praise.

narration.text: We remember negative feedback far more clearly than praise.
This happens because our brains have a negativity bias.
It is an ancient survival mechanism.
Our ancestors needed to quickly learn from dangers.
Threats meant survival, so negative events were prioritised.
This means bad experiences stick in our memory.
It is why a single criticism can outweigh many compliments.
Have you noticed this negativity bias in your own life?

description: Ever wonder why a single piece of bad news can overshadow a day of good experiences? Our brains are wired to remember negative events more vividly. This video explains the science behind the negativity bias.
topic: why bad news sticks in memory longer than good news
